security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by documented credential handling, expected output writes, Markdown formatting, and shell-safe FFmpeg calls. Confirmed risks involve external transmission of prompts and photos, unrestricted endpoint configuration, and unvalidated remote downloads. No prompt injection or malicious system-reconnaissance intent was found.

remediation.issue: Bearer credentials and user media can be sent to any MINIMAX_API_BASE value.
remediation.suggestion: Require HTTPS and allowlist official MiniMax API hosts, or require explicit confirmation before using a custom host.

remediation.issue: API-provided media URLs are downloaded without destination or size validation.
remediation.suggestion: Validate HTTPS hosts and redirects, stream downloads, set byte limits, and reject private or loopback destinations.

remediation.issue: The workflow sends personal photos to an external generation provider.
remediation.suggestion: Obtain explicit user consent and disclose the provider, purpose, and applicable retention policy before uploading images.

content.user_title: Create Animated GIF Stickers from Photos
content.value_statement: Turning photos into consistent animated stickers requires several generation and conversion steps. This skill coordinates MiniMax and FFmpeg to produce four captioned GIFs.
actual_capabilities: Creates four square sticker images from a person, pet, object, or logo description.
Uses a person photo as a character reference for facial likeness.
Generates short image-to-video animations through the MiniMax API.
Converts generated MP4 files into palette-optimized GIF files with FFmpeg.
Supports custom captions or default captions in seven languages.
Runs independent image and video generation jobs concurrently when the agent supports parallel execution.
limitations: Requires a MiniMax API key, a configured API base URL, Python dependencies, and FFmpeg.
Reference-image likeness is supported only for person subjects.
Generated media quality, text stability, latency, and cost depend on MiniMax services.
The workflow produces four GIFs and does not provide an interactive sticker editor.

use_cases.title: Build Personal Reaction Stickers
use_cases.description: Convert a portrait into four animated reactions with short captions for everyday messaging.

use_cases.title: Create Branded Animated Assets
use_cases.description: Turn a logo or product mascot into a consistent set of animated promotional stickers.

use_cases.title: Produce Multilingual Emoji Packs
use_cases.description: Generate captioned sticker sets that match the audience language across supported caption presets.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Default Sticker Pack
prompt_templates.prompt: Create four animated GIF stickers from this photo. Use the default captions for my language.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner wants the standard four reactions.

prompt_templates.title: Use Custom Captions
prompt_templates.prompt: Create four animated stickers from this pet photo. Use these captions: {caption_1}, {caption_2}, {caption_3}, and {caption_4}.
prompt_templates.scenario: A user wants personalized sticker text.

prompt_templates.title: Animate a Brand Mascot
prompt_templates.prompt: Transform this logo into four animated mascot stickers. Preserve its colors and shape. Use these actions: {actions}.
prompt_templates.scenario: A designer needs branded messaging assets.

prompt_templates.title: Control the Full Sticker Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a four-sticker pack from {subject}. Use {language}, captions {captions}, actions {actions}, and filenames {filenames}. Keep every caption readable.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user specifies localization, motion, and delivery details.

output_examples.input: Create the default English reaction stickers from my portrait.
output_examples.output: Four animated GIFs: a waving Hi sticker, laughing LOL sticker, crying Boo-hoo sticker, and heart-gesture Love ya sticker.

output_examples.input: Make a Spanish sticker pack from my pet photo.
output_examples.output: Four animated pet stickers with Spanish captions: Hola, Jajaja, Buaaa, and Te quiero.

output_examples.input: Animate our logo as a mascot with custom captions.
output_examples.output: Four square GIF stickers that preserve the logo colors and pair each supplied caption with a matching motion.

best_practices: Use a clear, well-lit reference photo with one visible subject.
Keep captions between one and three words for reliable rendering.
Confirm the target language, API endpoint, output paths, and estimated service cost before generation.
anti_patterns: Do not upload personal photos without the subject's consent.
Do not mix caption languages within one sticker pack.
Do not use untrusted API base URLs or unverified media download hosts.

faq.question: How many stickers does the skill create?
faq.answer: It creates four animated GIF stickers per workflow.

faq.question: Which subjects are supported?
faq.answer: It supports people, pets, objects, logos, and icons. Facial reference matching is limited to people.

faq.question: Can I provide my own captions?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide four short captions, preferably one to three words each.

faq.question: Which languages have default captions?
faq.answer: Defaults are included for English, Spanish, French, German, Chinese, Japanese, and Korean.

faq.question: What software and credentials are required?
faq.answer: You need Python, the requests package, FFmpeg, MINIMAX_API_KEY, and MINIMAX_API_BASE.

faq.question: Are my photos processed locally?
faq.answer: No. Reference images are encoded and sent to the configured MiniMax-compatible API for generation.
